best_for: Illustrators, comic artists and hobby painters with a drawing tablet who want a full painting studio without paying for a subscription.
description:
Krita is a painting program made by artists who want good art tools to be affordable for everyone. It is a public project owned by its contributors, many of them volunteers around the world. Users who want to help can pay into its development fund.

You can move and rearrange more than 30 panels, then save the layout as your own workspace, and set shortcuts for the tools you use most. For comics, drag a word bubble from the vector library onto the page and add text. Mix vector, filter, group and file layers in one picture. Import brush and texture packs from other artists, or bundle your own to share. If you know Python, you can write your own tools and panels.

points.title: No trial, no subscription
points.text: Krita is free and open source under the GPL v3, with no trial period or usage limits. The paid listings on the Microsoft Store, Steam, Epic and the Mac App Store are the same program with automatic updates, and the money goes to development.

points.title: Built for painting, not photo editing
points.text: It ships over 100 brushes across more than nine brush engines, stroke stabilizers, perspective and ellipse assistants, and a wrap-around mode for repeating tile patterns. Its tools center on drawing and painting from scratch.

points.title: Frame-by-frame animation included
points.text: A separate animation workspace has onion skinning, tweening, audio import and export to video or image sequences. Small studios can storyboard and animate without a second app.

points.title: Opens and saves PSD
points.text: Krita reads and writes Photoshop PSD files, so you can trade layered files with people who use Photoshop. It also handles HDR and EXR images with OpenColorIO and ICC color management.

points.title: Hardware to plan for
points.text: Krita asks for Windows 8.1 or later, macOS 10.15 or Linux, 4 GB of RAM (16 GB recommended) and a GPU with OpenGL 3.0 or Direct3D 11. New Windows builds are 64-bit only; 4.4.3 was the last 32-bit release.

points.title: Linux: AppImage or Flatpak
points.text: Krita's own Linux download is an AppImage. The Flatpak listed here is marked verified on Flathub, though Krita's download page describes the Flatpak as community-maintained. iPad and iPhone are not supported.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 32 versions of the machine-wide installer. macOS (one universal .dmg) and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need Krita's own archive of old versions.
